articles.title_orig: Anthropic shares tumble below $83 IPO price, on track to lose nearly $200 billion in value
articles.title_zh: Anthropic shares tumble below $83 IPO price, on track to lose nearly $200 billion in value
articles.content_orig:
Shares of Anthropic fell 8% on Tuesday, sending the stock below the artificial intelligence company's $83 IPO price.
The AI lab's stock has been sinking steadily since opening at $111.50 on the Nasdaq on Thursday, after Anthropic raised $81.3 billion in the largest offering of all time. Investors eagerly awaited Anthropic's debut in hopes that the company would revitalize the broader AI trade, which has been volatile in recent weeks over concerns about the feasibility of a multitrillion-dollar infrastructure buildout.
Anthropic's initial public offering was oversubscribed, and roughly half of the institutional investors that placed orders for the stock were left empty-handed, as CNBC previously reported . But at least for now, as the market wavers, those firms don't appear to be racing to scoop up shares.
Chip stocks Nvidia , Advanced Micro Devices and Intel , as well as neoclouds CoreWeave , IREN and Nebius , all fell during intraday trading on Tuesday. The market is still reeling after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, a dramatic reversal from his ouster earlier this month. Nvidia shares surged more than 30% on Monday, but pared those gains Tuesday.
Analysts at Canaccord Genuity said Tuesday that they're focused on Anthropic's long-term potential. They said they believe that the company is building "one of the most important enterprise technology franchises of the AI era" and that the "opportunity is considerably larger than traditional software spending."
Canaccord Genuity initiated coverage of Anthropic with a buy rating and a $135 price target.
"The risks are unusually large, particularly around infrastructure commitments and the durability of competitive differentiation, but we believe the combination of exceptional growth, emerging earnings capacity, and an attractive entry valuation support a compelling investment opportunity," the analysts wrote in a Tuesday note.
Wedbush analysts initiated coverage of Anthropic with an outperform rating and a $120 price target on Monday. They said Anthropic went public in a "tumultuous market" as debate around the AI buildout continues, but that they expect the company to navigate the competitive environment and "capture a uniquely large addressable market."
"While there's going to continue to be many ups and downs, and winners and losers as this ecosystem gets built, in our view there is no real question that it does get built over time," the analysts wrote in a Monday note. "The genie is out of the bottle. And ANT is a strong play on that theme."
Analysts at Oppenheimer initiated coverage of Anthropic with an outperform rating on Tuesday, and they set a $150 price target for the stock.
They said their "bullish stance" on the company stems from their belief that Anthropic will capture growing enterprise AI spending, that its improving compute efficiency lowers cost per task and that its multi-chip strategy optimizes price performance. The analysts added that Anthropic's focus on the enterprise also relies less on consumer subsidies, and that rising customer adoption creates "a substantial runway" for the company.
"While competition and compute commitments remain risks, we believe Anthropic can translate its leadership into durable growth and operating leverage," the analysts wrote in a Tuesday note.

articles.title_orig: Trump shares meme of Jensen Huang raising red bra in air
articles.title_zh: Trump shares meme of Jensen Huang raising red bra in air
articles.content_orig:
Jensen Huang is back as the CEO of Nvidia , and is now tasked with selling the company's artificial intelligence vision while also defending himself in Washington.
As Nvidia employees celebrated the return of their leader to the company's headquarters, Huang told the gathered crowd, "I'll be a better CEO the second time around."
Huang will need to be a better CEO to head off the issues surrounding Nvidia and the broader AI industry exposed by Huang's exit. The challenges include a proliferating roster of investigations and hearings from Congress, regulators and state-level officials , as well as technical and competitive questions about how long Nvidia's currently dominant graphics processing units can remain on top.
"There's nothing prohibiting him from doing what he does on his day job," said Katten chair and former federal prosecutor Gil Soffer. But investigations take significant prep time, Soffer said. "You don't just walk in cold."
At Nvidia's GTC conference in Washington, D.C., next week, the company will attempt to convince customers, partners and suppliers that it is developing the future of AI. At the same time, lawmakers will be pressing its newly reinstated CEO over what he knew and when about Megaspeed executive Alice Huang .
Huang, before his scandals, was scheduled to give the GTC DC keynote speech on Dec. 1 to discuss new Nvidia products and the trajectory of the AI ecosystem. In the past, the two-hour speech was the highlight of the event with hordes of fans full of the Huang-inspired "Jensanity."
"People will want to see that it's business as usual, which hopefully for Nvidia shareholders will mean that Jensen Huang announces some new exciting products," said Babson College associate professor Peter Cohan.
Right now, Nvidia has Ian Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing, filling the slot. A representative for Nvidia declined to answer multiple questions about whether Huang would appear at the company's event.
On the same day, Huang is scheduled to speak with three House committees — Foreign Affairs, Select Committee on the CCP, and the Select Committee on Intelligence — behind closed doors, where his interview will be transcribed.
"The NVIDIA board's brief internal investigation and reinstatement of Jensen Huang do not erase the national security threats and questions that must be addressed," the chairs said in a joint statement. They said that Huang has confirmed he will appear for the transcribed interview on Dec. 1.
Next Tuesday's interviews are just the first of a slew of investigations.
On Dec. 3, just as Nvidia's conference is wrapping up, the Senate Banking Committee will hold a hearing titled "Protecting America's AI Advantage: Oversight of U.S. Export Controls." Sen. Tim Scott, R-S.C., who chairs the committee, said Huang will publicly testify as the sole witness.
California's attorney general is also investigating Huang's remarks, and politicians from the Senate Finance, Intelligence, and Foreign Relations committees have inquired about the scandal. In the House, Energy and Commerce has requested a company briefing from Nvidia, in addition to the three committees mentioned earlier. That's not counting an investigation from the Department of Justice and a reported investigation from the Securities and Exchange Commission .
Plus, Huang still has to cooperate with an investigation from the board of directors, led by the law firm Wachtell Lipton.
Meanwhile, Nvidia needs Huang to reassure investors and the broader AI ecosystem that the company is developing new products that will be in high demand. Investors had said that while Nvidia's products for the next two years have been fully designed, they were worried that the chipmaker's pace of innovation would slow without Huang.
Nvidia is facing new competition from chips from its biggest customers, including OpenAI , Anthropic , Google , Amazon and Microsoft . The companies have been developing their own chips to reduce reliance on Nvidia, as well as to control AI costs.
"There was already this worry that we're spending too much on it," said Stephanie Balaouras, vice president of group research at Forrester. "One of those cost management strategies is to match ... the workload requirements to the right infrastructure. You don't need to put everything on a Nvidia GPU."
Many in the AI industry see Huang as one of the staunchest defenders of "open-source" AI that is free to use for commercial purposes, as compared with "frontier models" from companies like Anthropic and OpenAI, which charge users by the token.
Nvidia has also been spending heavily to develop its own open-source models called Nemotron. Currently, Nvidia Vice President Kari Briski is scheduled to present new Nemotron technology at GTC.
On Monday, Nvidia's board said that "senior levels" of the U.S. government provided input on Huang's potential national security risk. President Donald Trump told CNBC that he was central to convincing Nvidia's board to reinstate Huang and said he gave the board assurances.
Trump's help could draw even more scrutiny from Democratic lawmakers, who were already focused on probing Nvidia's chip sales.
"Today's news that Donald Trump engineered the rehiring of Jensen Huang at Nvidia is Exhibit A about the political corruption and rot at the heart of the Trump administration's big tech and AI policy," said Democratic Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland in a call with reporters Monday.
Republicans have also criticized Huang's return as the focus on the company's China sales intensifies. Still, the investigations could start to weigh on Nvidia's CEO, experts say.
"How could he possibly do the job?" Jeff Sonnenfeld , senior associate dean at the Yale School of Management, told CNBC, citing Senate investigations, House investigations and other state investigations, even before Democrats take over next year.
And the reaction in Washington to Huang's scandal could start to affect Nvidia's sales.
Last week, the Department of Commerce announced that it will prevent Chinese companies from getting around export controls by renting Nvidia's chips across borders. On Monday, Commerce also added Megaspeed to a trade blacklist.
And it's not just Nvidia that is relying on a strong performance from Huang. The company's investors, customers, partners and shareholders will also look to see if Nvidia still wants to be at the center of the AI ecosystem. Before Huang was removed, he pushed Nvidia to invest in AI startups, while selling them products, and helping finance their infrastructure.
Remarks from Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress last week while she was interim CEO suggested that Nvidia would be taking a "very strong look" at using its balance sheet to support the AI ecosystem, but it's unclear if Huang's second stint as CEO will continue with his prior showmanship or abide by a more measured approach.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia CEO Faces Senate Scrutiny Over China Chip and Spy Scandal
articles.title_zh: Nvidia CEO Faces Senate Scrutiny Over China Chip and Spy Scandal
articles.content_orig:
Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of AI tech giant Nvidia effective immediately following a scandal involving an alleged spy, the company's board of directors announced Thursday.
The decision came amid an investigation into Huang's affair with a woman U.S. intelligence agencies suspect was spying for China. President Trump said this week the FBI is investigating romantic and business ties between Huang and suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang. The two aren't related.
Nvidia's board had been preparing to oust Huang , two sources familiar with the matter confirmed to CBS News on Wednesday night, plans that were first reported by the Wall Street Journal.
Huang's departure also follows a New York Times report Wednesday that five employees at Nvidia came forward alleging Huang was romantically involved with a subordinate, Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare.
The Times also reported Huang and Powell, who are both married to other people, were caught on video being affectionate at a conference in March, according to two Nvidia employees. The Times has not seen the video and CBS News has not verified the report.
After Huang's resignation was announced Thursday, the Reuters news agency reported that Huang also had an intimate relationship with a second employee, according to two people familiar with the matter. The agency only identified the employee as a woman.
The company's interim CEO will be Colette Kress, who is currently Nvidia's chief financial officer and will continue in that role.
"The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption," Harvey Jones, who was announced as the company's first board chair, said in a statement.
Kress has been Nvidia's CFO since she joined the company in 2013. She previously worked in finance roles at tech companies like Cisco and Microsoft for nearly 25 years.
Nvidia was co-founded by Huang in 1993. It became one of the most valuable companies in the world by designing the powerful semiconductors that fuel many of the world's leading AI firms, making its technology highly sensitive and subject to export controls limiting sales to China.
Nvidia's stock plunged as news emerged of the company's turmoil, potentially erasing almost $500 billion in value. In Thursday's trading, the stock price closed down 4.3% at $166.19.
Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was an executive at Megaspeed International , a Singapore-based data center company whose website touts its partnership with Nvidia.
Megaspeed grew with the help of access to Nvidia's restricted AI computer chips. According to U.S. investigators, Alice Huang was able to gain access to 240,000 chips that were banned from being exported to China. Megaspeed is under investigation in the U.S. and Singapore for allegedly smuggling those chips into China.
In Washington, top Democrats on Capitol Hill have expressed concerns over whether Jensen Huang's ties to Alice Huang may have compromised U.S. national security.
Following Jensen Huang's resignation, Democratic Sen. Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts said his departure doesn't absolve him or the company from the scandal.
"Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and NVIDIA's board of directors still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Warren said in a statement.
Before Huang resigned, Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co., told CBS News the departure could help China in the competition between Beijing and the U.S.
"With him out as CEO, China could significantly narrow the gap versus the U.S.," Ives said. He added: "The problem now is that there's no replacement for Jensen. It's a black eye moment for him, for Nvidia, and actually the U.S. tech industry. I'd say it's dark day for, you know, U.S. technology."
Following Thursday morning's announcement, Mr. Trump said on his Truth Social platform that there was "only one man" who could replace Huang: former Apple CEO Tim Cook .
Mr. Trump had a close relationship with Huang, who has attended AI-focused White House events and traveled with Mr. Trump to China. Late last year, Mr. Trump granted Nvidia the right to sell advanced H200 chips to "approved customers" in China, with the U.S. government getting a 25% cut — a major coup for Huang, who has long sought to sell more technology to the Chinese market. The deal did not cover Nvidia's even more advanced Blackwell and Rubin systems.
In a radio interview Thursday, Mr. Trump brought up that he gave Huang a National Medal of Science earlier this year. "What a horrible thing that is," he said of the situation involving Huang, adding, "That's so sad to see that happen."
In a statement accompanying her appointment as interim CEO, Kress said that the company's focus will be on "serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders."
"NVIDIA's strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years," Kress said.
The board said it will be conducting a search for a permanent CEO and will consider internal and external candidates.
Isabel  Vincent , Jennifer  Jacobs , Aimee  Picchi and Jo Ling  Kent contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: No more heated seat subscriptions for cars in New York from 2027
articles.title_zh: No more heated seat subscriptions for cars in New York from 2027
articles.content_orig:
Car buyers in New York may find the cost of ownership reduces a little next year. Maybe. Governor Kathy Hochul signed a bill yesterday that bans car companies and dealerships from locking up car features behind a subscription, a law that goes into effect on February 27 next year.
“People spending their hard-earned money on a car shouldn’t have to fork over even more money for features that should automatically come with the car. My message to car companies is clear: this kind of deceptive business model isn’t going to fly in New York State. Keep your hands out of New Yorkers’ wallets,” the governor said.
In the old days, the only options you paid to use after you bought a car were mods or upgrades you installed after the fact. That started to change with services like General Motors’ OnStar, which introduced telematics to the vehicle—for a monthly fee.
We end users might not like having to open our wallets each month, but the capital markets sure do, and car companies love making the capital markets happy. Which is why there has been such a push toward connected vehicles. Remote start and predictive maintenance alerts are nice, but your regular payments to the car company— plus any data of yours it can sell —is the goal.
Some automakers have gone even further. Infamously, BMW and its heated seats. Like the McDonald’s coffee lawsuit, it’s a fact half-remembered; BMW North America never tried such a thing, just in countries like South Korea and the UK , and in 2023 BMW’s board said that subscriptions would only be for software-related features from then on.
New York’s press release mentions heated seats but also calls out a number of other modern tech features: “enhanced navigation, hands-free driving and entertainment options that do not present an ongoing expense for dealers and manufacturers.”
But the way the actual law is written appears to leave a rather large loophole, at least to these eyes.
S.9348A/A.10411A prohibits motor vehicle manufacturers, dealers or third-party service providers from adding subscription services or charging post-purchase fees for any motor vehicle feature that uses pre-installed components or hardware that do not have an ongoing cost. As vehicles become more advanced, the new law aims to establish clear rules preventing exploitative practices and prevent post-purchase fees as a future automotive business model.
A heated seat might not have “an ongoing cost,” but the maps and databases that enable “enhanced navigation” and “hands-free driving” systems definitely do, as these need to be constantly updated. A regular cadence of software updates also generates an ongoing cost to an OEM, arguably. And car companies pay for plenty of lawyers who really love to argue.
And so, while experiments like BMW’s seat heater subscription won’t be allowed in the state, the new rule might still allow for plenty of ongoing fees for services like OnStar or Mercedes’ Drive Assist Pro system we tested recently .

articles.title_orig: Trump administration tees up tariff hikes on EU, China, others
articles.title_zh: Trump administration tees up tariff hikes on EU, China, others
articles.content_orig:
The U.S. trade representative's office is set to unveil its latest tariff plans Tuesday night.
The Trump administration will propose new tariff hikes Tuesday night on the European Union, China, Mexico, Japan and 12 other trading partners, a major step towards recreating the president’s global duties the Supreme Court struck down in February.
According to one person with knowledge of the planning, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer will announce the new tariff proposals as part of a report into the countries’ excess manufacturing capacity. The findings are the product of a trade investigation Greer’s office launched in March under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which allows the U.S. trade representative to impose tariffs in response to unfair trade practices.
Three other people briefed by the administration on the investigation confirmed the report was in the process of being finalized and the results would be announced as soon as today. They were granted anonymity to share details of policy plans that are not yet public.
The Wall Street Journal first reported the announcement was coming.

articles.title_orig: Trump’s intervention on Huang will exact ‘heavy cost’ on rule of law, national security: WSJ editorial board
articles.title_zh: Trump’s intervention on Huang will exact ‘heavy cost’ on rule of law, national security: WSJ editorial board
articles.content_orig:
His accounts continued to trade Nvidia in recent months, according to filings.
President Donald Trump owned at least $12 million in Nvidia stock at the end of 2025, according to his annual financial disclosure report reviewed by ABC News.
His accounts have continued to trade Nvidia in recent months, including more than three dozen trades buying and selling millions of dollars of Nvidia stock this year through September, according to separate filings that disclose trades in his accounts.
The White House continues to maintain that third-party institutions manage Trump's accounts.
"President Trump's stock and bond portfolio is independently managed by third-party financial institutions. All holdings are maintained in discretionary accounts and invested through computer-based model portfolios that automatically replicate recognized indexes, such as the Schwab 1000," said White House spokesperson Davis Ingle.
"Neither President Trump nor any member of his family has any ability to direct, influence, or provide input regarding how the portfolio is invested or when investments are bought or sold. All investment decisions are made entirely by independent managers."
Trump has repeatedly vouched for Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang amid the scandal surrounding his alleged afair with a woman U.S. intelligence alleges is a Chinese asset.
On Monday, he took credit for Huang's stunning return to Nvidia , saying in an interview that he spoke "directly and indirectly" to the company's board members about bringing Huang back as CEO.
"I spoke to them. Let me put it this way: And I convinced them. I made the deal," Trump, who had urged Huang's reinstatement publicly, said in a phone interview with CNBC .
Following the announcement, the major stock indexes rebounded sharply on Monday as Nvidia shares closed up more than 30%.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed up 1,447.98 points, or 3.0%, while the S & P 500 jumped over 4.73%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq soared over 6.5%.
Shares of Nvidia surged, recovering nearly all of the losses suffered since Nov. 12, the day Nvidia announced Huang's resignation .
Nvidia develops the semiconductor chips, systems, and software powering artificial intelligence. In early October 2026, its market valuation reached $5.8 trillion.
Given its significant presence in the stock market, Nvidia is a common holding in many investment portfolios and Trump's shares in the company represent a small portion of his overall portfolio.

articles.title_orig: CF40 Research: China’s real estate adjustment may be nearing its end—and its external surplus could stop widening
articles.title_zh: CF40 Research: China’s real estate adjustment may be nearing its end—and its external surplus could stop widening
articles.content_orig:
Late last month, CF40 Research , the research arm of the China Finance 40 Forum-a leading non-governmental think tank specializing in economics, shared its annual flagship report, China’s Economy: Toward a New Paradigm—Drivers, Trends, and Policy Implications , at its 2026 Bund Summit .
Guo Kai , President of CF40 Research and a former Chinese central bank official, kindly shared a copy and allowed me to share an excerpt.
The following passages are from the report’s English text. They have been rearranged and intervening material omitted; section headings and this introduction are mine. Corporate debt and profit figures below refer to its sample of A-share-listed companies outside finance and petroleum.
By 2026, the current real estate adjustment may not yet have fully run its course, but signs of structural stabilization have begun to emerge. After five years of deep adjustment, housing sales, investment, inventories, and developers’ balance sheets have entered a new phase, while house-price declines have begun to moderate. Few would expect the real estate sector to return to its former “golden age,” but the drag from the ongoing adjustment on the economy has diminished markedly at the margin. In other words, real estate is gradually shifting from the economy’s largest source of downward pressure toward a more stable influence.
Based on our analysis of international real estate corrections, China’s current real estate adjustment has already been considerable in both duration and magnitude, and the market has likely entered a bottoming phase. Further adjustment remains possible, but another sharp contraction appears unlikely.
Since the start of 2026, China’s real estate market has begun to show signs of “structural stabilization.” We selected 33 core cities for analysis, including the four first-tier cities—Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, and Shenzhen—and major second-tier cities such as Hangzhou, Suzhou, Qingdao, Wuhan, and Hefei. We find that house prices, the floor area of new homes sold, and existing-home transaction volumes have all shown signs of stabilizing in these cities. House prices have even risen modestly in a few core cities. By contrast, real estate markets in most third- and fourth-tier cities remain weak. In other words, stabilization is concentrated in core cities rather than broad-based, which is why we refer to it as “structural stabilization.”
Thus, for the 33 core cities, if new starts continue to decline sharply, excess housing inventory could be rapidly reduced, potentially giving way to a shortage. This would provide additional support for house prices and demand and could accelerate the housing market’s recovery.
Over the past few years, the deep adjustment in the real estate market has been the main driver of the widening current account surplus. The underlying mechanism is that the real estate downturn led to a sharp decline in the investment rate, while the saving rate adjusted with a lag. The resulting widening of the saving–investment gap translated directly into a larger current account surplus.
As the real estate market gradually stabilizes, the drag from real estate investment will diminish, while household precautionary saving will stop rising. The saving–investment gap will therefore narrow, and the current account surplus will stabilize at a high level rather than continue to widen. This process bears some resemblance to the decline in China’s current account surplus after 2008, when the RMB 4 trillion stimulus package drove a sharp expansion in domestic investment, significantly narrowing the saving–investment gap.
By contrast, the stabilization of the manufacturing capacity cycle since 2024 has clearly not relied on comparable demand-side stimulus. Instead, the sequence has been “supply adjustment first, followed by a moderate recovery in demand”: a market-driven process in which firms voluntarily slowed investment and retired inefficient capacity in response to weak demand. This differs fundamentally from the post-2016 cyclical reversal driven by a sharp rebound in demand.
According to CF40 research, the new economy’s total value added rose from about 6.1% of GDP in 2018 to 10.4% in 2025, while the corresponding share for real estate fell from 12.7% to 8.4%. By 2025, the new economy’s total value-added share had surpassed that of real estate and had become an important component of GDP.
A defining characteristic of new-economy firms is their greater emphasis on R&D and their ability to generate more operating revenue and profits with less debt. In 2025, new-economy firms accounted for only 11.9% of the total interest-bearing debt of firms in the full sample, compared with 17.8% of total operating revenue and 29.5% of total net profits across the sample. Their share of total R&D expenditure was even higher, at 47.6%. As the new economy accounts for a growing share of China’s economy, the country’s growth model will gradually evolve.
The negative wealth effect of the real estate adjustment is fading, but households’ propensity to consume remains well below its pre-pandemic level, while further improvements in social security and public services are constrained by fiscal pressures. Rather than rising sharply, the consumption rate is therefore more likely to stabilize as the drag from real estate fades. If supportive policies are fully implemented, the consumption rate could gradually rise.
Moreover, the more advanced a manufacturing industry, the lower the share of output going to compensation of employees tends to be. For example, compensation of employees accounts for only 7.8% and 7.6% of gross output in electrical machinery and equipment manufacturing and automobile manufacturing, respectively—two industries that together encompass the “new three.” The corresponding share is 8.7% in computer, communications, and other electronic equipment manufacturing, the industry most closely associated with AI.
On a value-added basis, compensation of employees accounts for 36%, 42%, and 47% in these three industries, respectively, all below the service-sector average. This means that even if the new economy continues to expand rapidly and drive economic growth, households’ share of income in primary distribution will not automatically increase and could even decline. This is because these new-economy industries allocate a smaller share of their output to compensation of employees than the current economy-wide average.
On monetary policy, emphasis should move further away from pursuing credit-volume expansion toward lowering interest rates, improving inflation expectations, and restoring nominal demand. Real estate no longer performs its previous role in credit expansion, while the new economy is relatively less dependent on bank credit. Growth in bank lending and total social financing is therefore increasingly difficult to use on its own as a measure of whether monetary policy is sufficiently accommodative.
One possible aggregate benchmark is that “nominal growth in broad fiscal expenditure should exceed nominal GDP growth.” At present, local governments face multiple constraints, including declining land-related revenues, debt resolution efforts, and rising mandatory spending commitments. Near-term fiscal expansion will therefore need to rely more heavily on the central government.
The new economy has demonstrated China’s capacity to create new productive capacity, but the more important issue for the next stage is how to translate that capacity into household income and final consumption. New-economy firms have high R&D spending, high productivity, and low reliance on debt—an important direction for economic transformation. However, if the industrial structure merely shifts from traditional manufacturing toward more advanced manufacturing, higher productivity will not necessarily translate automatically into a larger household income share or a higher consumption rate.

articles.title_orig: Israeli air strike kills Hamas internal security chief in Gaza
articles.title_zh: Israeli air strike kills Hamas internal security chief in Gaza
articles.content_orig:
At least seven Palestinians, including a senior Hamas security official, have been killed in Israeli air strikes in the Gaza Strip, health officials and first responders say.
Naeem Abu Nahel, the head of Hamas's internal security service, was targeted in western Gaza City, Gaza's Hamas-run interior ministry said. The 50-year-old had only been in the position since September, when his predecessor was captured in a raid by Israeli special forces .
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz announced that Abu Nahel was "eliminated" by the Israeli military.
The six other people were killed in two earlier air strikes elsewhere in Gaza.
Three people, including a teenage boy, were killed in the Wadi Gaza area, south of Gaza City, according to the health officials and first responders. The other three were killed at a police station in the al-Mawasi area, west of Khan Younis, they added.
Gaza's police force, which operates under the interior ministry, said two of its officers were among those who died in the second attack. It also accused Israel of "an ongoing campaign targeting the police apparatus aimed at sowing chaos" in the territory.
The Israeli military said it struck "military operatives" in both areas.
Witnesses said an Israeli drone targeted Naeem Abu Nahel as he was walking on a side street near a tent camp for displaced people in Gaza City.
Several other people were reportedly seriously injured in the strike.
The Israeli military said Abu Nahel had "possessed extensive institutional knowledge" about Hamas's internal security service - which is responsible for enforcing discipline, protecting infrastructure and rooting out informants - and that his death constituted "a blow to the apparatus's management capabilities".
It also alleged that he had advanced attacks on Israeli troops and civilians during the war and that it killed him "to remove the threat he posed".
Gaza's interior ministry said Abu Nahel's killing followed what it described as the internal security service's "important achievements in combating gangs collaborating with the occupation [Israel] and operating in areas under the control of its military".
Violence has continued in Gaza since Israel and Hamas agreed to a US-brokered ceasefire in October last year. Israeli strikes take place almost daily in areas under Hamas's control, which are home to 2.1 million people, most of them displaced.
At least 1,679 people have been killed in Gaza over the past 13 months, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.
Israel says six of its soldiers have been killed in Gaza during the same period.
The humanitarian situation also remains dire, with heavy rainfall earlier this month causing flooding and damage to thousands of shelters for displaced families.
The UN and its partners have called on Israel - which controls Gaza's crossings - to allow in more supplies to help Palestinians prepare for the winter, including tents, heaters and water pumps, as well as vaccines and medicines to combat infectious diseases.
On Tuesday, the health ministry warned that there had been a rapid rise in cases of meningitis, with 272 reported in October - about eight times the usual monthly average.
Fifteen deaths had been attributed to the infection so far this year, including five reported between August and October, it said.
Israeli military body Cogat said on Monday it was "working to provide a dedicated humanitarian response" and that a newly approved package of pumps, generators, water tankers and medical equipment had been presented at a meeting with UN agencies.
The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.
Since then, more than 74,740 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza, the health ministry says.

articles.title_orig: Gisèle Pelicot to sue publisher that sent nude images to media, says she's "once again humiliated"
articles.title_zh: Gisèle Pelicot to sue publisher that sent nude images to media, says she's "once again humiliated"
articles.content_orig:
Gisèle Pelicot, the French woman who spoke out about being drugged and raped by her husband and dozens of other men, said Monday that she had been "once again humiliated" after nude photos and videos of her were sent to media outlets to promote a book that she said is dismissive of her husband's crimes.
Pelicot, 73, told France's BFMTV that she will take legal action against the publisher, Tinard, and the author of the book, French psychoanalyst Sabine Prokhoris.
The book criticizes the concept of coercive control and questions whether Pelicot was really a victim, suggesting she could have been complicit in her husband's actions despite her having been surreptitiously drugged for years.
"I am deeply shocked that images relating to my most intimate life could be exhibited and exploited for commercial purposes," Pelicot said in a statement to the French broadcaster, adding: "Above all, I refuse to have my story rewritten by implying that I was complicit in what I suffered."
"Today, I find myself humiliated, exposed, and hurt once again. As if the ordeal of the trial wasn't enough," she said. "I fought to regain my dignity and my freedom. I will not let anyone take them away from me."
Pelicot became a global symbol of resilience in 2024 when she waived her right to anonymity in her then-husband Dominique's trial. He was convicted and sentenced to 20 years in prison for his abuse — and for inviting 50 other men to join him in raping his wife while she was incapacitated repeatedly over the course of a decade.
"How can you imagine that your husband is drugging you? It's unthinkable — impossible," she told CBS News in February. "In fact, I was manipulated for about 10 years. Because he was looking me in the eyes every day while knowing he was poisoning me. But I never saw that. I saw a kind, caring man."
She said she waived her anonymity during the trial to show that "shame has to change sides," from victims to perpetrators.
On its website, the publisher Tinard said it had offered "our sincerest apologies" to Pelicot and that it would not be reprinting the book after 280 copies already printed are sold. It said "no images of rape or pornographic videos were leaked to the press."
It is not clear where the publisher got the nude images of Pelicot. In her statements to French media, Pelicot did not question their authenticity. She also did not confirm or deny a report by the French weekly news outlet Le Canard Enchaîne, which said the images were among those taken by her former husband and presented during his trial as evidence.
Prokhoris, the author, said she had given "full responsibility" for the promotional campaign to the publisher, according to French news agency AFP.
AFP said the back-cover blurb on the book asks readers to "think freely" about the notion of coercive control, which Prokhoris describes as "a cornerstone of #MeToo orthodoxy" that is "fundamentally ambiguous" and, she says, involves "each of the parties in an equally responsible, though not symmetrical, way."
"There are two types of violence that have been committed," Pelicot's lawyer Christophe Bigot told BFM. "There is, on the one hand, the fact that intimate images of her were sent without her consent in the context of purely commercial communication, and then there is a book that calls into question her status as a victim."
"It is a clear violation of the law, and she does not intend to let it go unchallenged," he said.

When the game's reviews went live — including our own five-star review from Jez Corden — I knew that there was no way I could miss out on the fun of discovering an unexplored open world of this scale.
Just one problem. The gaming PC into which I've poured thousands of dollars is useless. No one knows when GTA 6 is actually coming to PC in an official capacity (barring some sketchy AI recompiles).
Not wanting to spend another $1,000+ on a Series X or PS5 just to play one game, I picked up an unused Xbox Series S my brother had lying around.
I thought I knew what I was getting myself into. I'd seen Digital Foundry's breakdown of performance on all consoles, including less-than-great results for the Series S. I know that the game runs at a maximum of 30 FPS no matter the console, a far cry from the 200+ FPS to which I'm accustomed on my PC.
About 30-40 hours of marathon gaming later (who needs sleep?), I'm ready to be brutally honest about what it's like going from PC to Series S for GTA 6 .
All Grand Theft Auto 6 images and videos in this article was captured on an Xbox Series S, unless otherwise stated.
Usually, if I see 30 FPS while gaming, I assume that something's wrong with my PC. On the Series S, 30 FPS is more of a goal than a baseline .
Despite running at a 720p native resolution that's then upscaled to 1080p with AMD's FSR 4 tech running behind the scenes, the Series S has a hard time remaining at 30 FPS when the action picks up.
👉 Xbox Series S FINALLY gets the respect it deserves — all thanks to GTA 6
Frame rates seem to move around quite freely between 20 and 30 FPS on the Series S when things get frenetic. It's a tough sell, to be sure, but at least everything feels a lot smoother when you're just cruising around and checking out the game's seemingly endless supply of content.
As a PC gamer, comparing performance at 20 to 30 FPS feels a bit like asking which piece of trash on the ground is least soggy . It's still going to feel gross, but at least you have something .
The Xbox Series X , PS5 , and PS5 Pro do at least bump the resolution up to 1440p , which is then upscaled to 4K , providing a sharper overall picture.
Am I regretting playing at the Series S's 720p resolution upscaled to 1080p, shown on a big 4K TV? Not at all.
I'm used to precision controls without input latency. Switching to a gamepad on a console running at 30 FPS or less makes me feel like I've already had a full case of Pindayho cold ones while seated on my couch.
Driving and shooting, two of the game's primary activities, take a lot of getting used to because of input latency .
Good news, though. By the end of my first marathon session, I'd basically stopped noticing input latency at all. I'm no longer regularly crashing my car or whiffing shots because of it. Back to blaming my own abilities with a gamepad.
I don't think I'll ever get used to the game's abysmal frame rate, but at least the input lag irons itself out in my brain. Oh, yeah, and don't forget that all consoles suffer from similar latency.
The first 10 hours of GTA 6 have me believing the game's stellar reviews. Despite using the weakest console to run it at a lower resolution, it's one of the most detailed and visually impressive games I've ever seen.
Some scenes border on photorealism , with Series S ray tracing doing an admirable job of making the bright Leonida coastline pop. I'm still sitting back and saying, "Whoa," after ten hours of play.
My colleague Ben Wilson grabbed some screenshots from the Series S and Series X to compare the visual fidelity. Use the slider on the images to check the difference; can you figure out which side is Series X and which one is Series S?
I don't think anyone will disagree that the Series X offers more detail, better ray tracing, and superior lighting. But the differences are so minor that they should not scare you away from the Series S.
When it eventually launches on PC, it will immediately be in the running for best-looking game of all time, if it isn't already.
Someone, somewhere, has already cooked up an " Xbox shill! " response to my GTA 6 on Series S impressions. That's fine. I couldn't care less what console you spend your time on. I'm a PC gamer, and I'm just here to relay what I've discovered so far on the Series S.
And what I have discovered so far is a mix of god-awful frame rates, frustrating input latency, and one of the most detailed, gorgeous virtual worlds ever created.
I don't think there's any one good reason to avoid the game on Series S.
Since this seems to be largely the fate of all consoles running GTA 6 , I don't think there's any one good reason to avoid the game on Series S. This is the first time I've touched a console in probably almost a decade, and it's truly impressive that this little white rectangle is spitting out what I'm seeing on my TV.
One last thing: for those who have an Xbox One lying around, the GTA 6 and Xbox Cloud Gaming experience is better than expected , giving those without a Series X|S another way to play.
Are you also enjoying GTA 6 on the Series S? What do you think about performance? About the game overall? Let me know in the comments section below!
"A game so good I asked our tech team if I could somehow give it 11/10. GTA 6 is an absolute masterclass in genre-mashing. With meticulous detailing and levels of immersion that almost feel dangerous, it's steeped in steamy satire — with story beats that often cut close to home as they relish in laugh-out-loud absurdity." - Jez Corden, Windows Central

articles.title_orig: GTA 6 Fashion Is Taking Social Media by Storm
articles.title_zh: GTA 6 Fashion Is Taking Social Media by Storm
articles.content_orig:
We've known for some time that fashion would be a big deal in Grand Theft Auto 6 . In Rockstar's official promotional materials for the game, both Jason and Lucia were prominently featured wearing stylish clothing, from Lucia's body-hugging gold dress to Jason's slick Miami Vice -inspired aqua sport coat. Even supporting characters like Brian wear Tommy Bahama-inspired aloha shirts yanked straight from the closet of a dapper middle-aged stoner. GTA 6 has drawn praise from all quarters for its scrupulous attention to detail in every aspect of the game, and there's one area the developer went far, far harder than it needed to: the vast and immaculate selection of T-shirts.
Having a diverse wardrobe isn't just a fun little customization touch in GTA 6. If you're reported for committing a crime in Leonida — and this will happen very often — police will be able to recognize you based on your car, your physical appearance, and what you're wearing. Keeping a couple spare outfits in your trunk or hastily buying a new ensemble on the run can be the difference between a successful job and ending up busted (or wasted).
I'm taking my time with GTA 6 and still kicking around the introductory area of Key Lento. I know I should be putting money in my family savings account. It would probably be in my best interest to learn how to drive without sideswiping semi-trucks or taking out stop signs. Perhaps I ought to be buying more guns. Instead, I'm trawling South Leonida for all the vintage and souvenir shops I can find. You can keep your fancy cars. I've got a T-shirt collection to maintain.
Much like in real life, you never know when you're going to find a gem in a vintage boutique or souvenir shop in GTA 6 . My prized Rusty Anchor shirt came from an optional mission where you take Cal for drinks, he has a few too many, and you have to take him home. Apparently Cal won a wet T-shirt contest at the Anchor and this was his reward, but he's too hungover to claim the prize.
During my wanderings, I also discovered a riff on that three-wolves-howling-at-the-moon shirt that everyone had about a decade ago, including me. But this one has gators on it. I bought it from Sharleen's yard sale in Jason's very own neighborhood of Key Lento. She had a couple of inexpensive clothing items on offer, including some pretty slick teal sneakers that were clearly inspired by Air Force One low-tops. I was delighted to learn that there are multiple yard sales in the game, including one in Port Gellhorn where you can buy a dupe of Arthur Morgan's hat from Red Dead Redemption 2 .
Even the cheesiest souvenir shops, like Leroy's in Key Lento, have the exact kind of "so bad it's good" T-shirts you'll see dozens of times over the course of a weekend in a tourist trap. Do I need to spend $38 of my ill-gotten dollars on a horrendous blue granny shirt with a dolphin on it, with "Vice Beach" written in collegiate font? Certainly not. But I am tempted.
Rockstar has a bunch of GTA 6 merch on its official website , including T-shirts, though much of it is currently sold out. Here's hoping they expand the offering with a couple of these in-game gems. If you're hard up for a three gator moon shirt though, you can already find them on Amazon and Etsy .

articles.title_orig: Denmark: Supreme Court backs hardline immigration law against 'non-Westerners'
articles.title_zh: Denmark: Supreme Court backs hardline immigration law against 'non-Westerners'
articles.content_orig:
Denmark's Supreme Court on Monday ruled in favor of a housing association that terminated 91 leases in order to prevent the label "hard ghetto" being applied to their housing complex. The decision align's with Copenhagen's hardline approach to immigration .
The court on Monday upheld Denmark 's 2018 "ghetto law," which allows for the relocation of "non-Western" residents from minority-heavy neighborhoods in order to foster integration . The Danish court ruling diverges from a top EU court decision last year that found application of the law could amount to discrimination.
The Danish laws requires social housing estates to rebuild, renovate and adjust their social mix if these become minority heavy, stipulating that 60% of apartments be rented to "Westerners" at market value by 2030.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Denmark's pioneering role in spearheading tougher immigration rules has made it a model for some in the EU . Denmark was also one of five countries that last week announced its intent to set up an asylum seeker deportation hub in Rwanda.
Danish Housing Minister Jacob Mark welcomed Monday's decision, saying it "strengthens security, social cohesion and integration."
The court's decision upheld a 2022 lower court ruling against seven tenants who fought their evictions in Nojsomhed, Helsingor, just north of Copenhagen.
In Monday's ruling, the law was found to be non-discriminatory when it comes to the eviction of "immigrants and descendants from non-Western countries" as it is not broadly based on ethnicity. The EU ruling focused on this particular aspect, saying the law would be discriminatory if criteria were race based, while ultimately allowing national courts to have the last say in the matter.
"The Supreme Court notes that applying the criterion of the law involves dividing people into two groups [immigrants and descendants from non-Western countries, and all other persons]. Both groups include a very large majority of different ethnic origins, and there will simultaneously be persons with the same ethnic origin in both groups," read the Danish court's ruling.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Tenants' associations estimate that 11,000 people across Denmark will have to be relocated to comply with the law.
The housing association in question issued a written statement saying that it was aware that the evictions would impact those affected, adding that it undertook measures to insure that residents found new homes.
According to Statistics Denmark's definition, "non-Western" countries include every country other than the 27 member states of the European Union, as well as Andorra, Australia, Britain, Canada, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, New Zealand, Northern Ireland, Norway, San Marino, Switzerland, the United States and the Vatican.

articles.title_orig: US lawmakers vow to investigate Jensen Huang and Trump over Nvidia scandal
articles.title_zh: US lawmakers vow to investigate Jensen Huang and Trump over Nvidia scandal
articles.content_orig:
The stock market was thrilled with the announcement that Jensen Huang was returning as CEO of Nvidia, but lawmakers on both sides of the aisle reacted with shock — and said they still expect him to answer questions next week on Capitol Hill .
“You gotta be kidding me,” Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, told MS NOW when he learned of Huang’s reinstatement 11 days after he resigned in the wake of revelations of alleged extramarital affairs, including one with a woman U.S. intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy.
In its announcement, the board said it reached the decision after receiving “input from senior levels of the United States government” that his “reinstatement poses no national security risk.”
“No national security risk? Based on what?” Cornyn asked in a post on X .
President Donald Trump told CNBC he’d spoken to the board “directly and indirectly.”
“One of the things the board wanted to know, is there a national security problem?” Trump said. “And after a lot of research, we — you know, we’ve been looking at this for more than a couple of days, right? This has been a story for a few weeks. We said no, it’s not a problem.”
Lawmakers made clear they still need answers.
The Senate Banking Committee, chaired by Sen. Tim Scott, R-S.C., announced that Huang was scheduled to testify publicly Dec. 3.
“The national security concerns and adherence to export controls will be central to the committee’s oversight and the congressional hearing. Our markets demand transparency. Americans deserve the truth. Our committee will deliver answers,” Scott said in a statement.
A spokesperson for the House Intelligence Committee told NBC News that Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia CEO “changes nothing” for the three House committees that are set to conduct a closed-door transcribed interview with Huang on Dec. 1.
“There are serious questions on national security implications that still need answers. Seems like the only thing that is consistent these days on this issue is our three Committee’s commitment to oversight,” the spokesperson said in a statement.
In a joint statement later Monday, the chairs of the House Select Committee on China, the Intelligence Committee and the House Foreign Affairs Committee said Huang and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter “have confirmed they will appear for their transcribed interviews on December 1 and December 2 as previously planned.”
“We remain committed to getting answers on the mass smuggling of NVIDIA products, their diversion for Chinese military purposes, and their key role in advancing our foremost adversary’s AI capabilities,” said the three Republicans, Reps. John Moolenaar of Michigan, Rick Crawford of Arkansas and Brian Mast of Florida.
The speedy reinstatement and assurances of the lack of a security risk came after the Justice and Commerce departments last week shared details about their investigation into Megaspeed , the Singapore-based company tied to Alice Huang , the suspected spy with whom Huang was allegedly involved.
Megaspeed reportedly acquired billions of dollars’ worth of Nvidia chips and is also being investigated over concerns that it — and its subsidiaries — smuggled chips to China.
Sen. Kevin Cramer, R-N.D., said in an X post that “the legal and reputational risk of hiring a CEO who may very well be convicted in the United States or other nations of violating espionage and export control laws is now born by the board of Nvidia, but the national security risk is passed along to the United States military and its citizens. The risk of extortion by a Chinese asset who’s been banned by Singapore is risk enough to not rehire Huang.”
Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., told NBC News in a phone interview “It’s not my job as a public official to tell a private company who to pick for their CEO. That’s up to the board of directors.”
But, he added, “What I want to know is whether Nvidia violated the export controls of our country with respect to advanced chips. And I want to know if the Department of Commerce did. That will be the purpose of the Banking Committee hearing.”
Sen. Jeanne Shaheen of New Hampshire, the top Democrat on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, said in a statement that the administration appears to have known about the Chinese espionage efforts targeting the Nvidia CEO for the past year and his reinstatement “without any apparent accounting or response to the risks to our national security, demands an explanation.”
Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., said the administration’s “rush to reinstate Jensen Huang underscores the need for Congress to act.”
“Trump is putting his own financial interests and the needs of his billionaire buddies before our national security, emphasizing that he’s learned nothing from his resounding election defeat,” Schumer said in a statement. He added that “Democrats will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump Administration, Jensen Huang, other NVIDIA executives, and anyone selling out our national security for financial gain.”
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., called the board’s decision “indefensible, irresponsible and incomprehensible.”
“Congress will not be deterred from conducting a swift, thorough and wide-ranging investigation into business malfeasance by NVIDIA and corrupt abuse of power by Howard Lutnick and the Department of Commerce,” Jeffries said.
Lutnick agreed earlier this month to testify before Congress about the Huang scandal amid lawmakers’ scrutiny of China’s access to advanced AI chips.
Democrats pointed Trump’s financial ties to Nvidia, with Rep. Robert Garcia of California, the ranking member on the Oversight Committee, noting the president has a sizeable amount of Nvidia stock. “No president who has invested in a private company should be involved in their board decisions,” Garcia said .
Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi, D-Ill., cited Nvidia’s donation to Trump’s White House ballroom project as a reason to give the board’s decision extra scrutiny.
“Trump’s assurances cannot be taken at face value, especially after Nvidia’s $25 million donation to his ballroom. Huang must testify at a full public congressional hearing, with every member of the relevant committees allowed to question him,” he posted on X.
Sen. Pete Ricketts, R-Neb., questioned the Nvidia board’s decision in a post on social media.
“Jensen Huang had multiple affairs including with subordinates and an alleged Chinese spy,” Ricketts wrote. “His own board described his behavior as lacking ‘candor.’ I’ve served on a public company board. His behavior does not support reinstatement.”
“Nvidia’s decision today doesn’t excuse Jensen Huang from testifying before Congress,” he continued. “It also doesn’t absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips. I look forward to Mr. Huang coming to the Senate in December.”
Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., called the president’s actions “Exhibit A about the political corruption and rot at the heart of the Trump administration’s big tech and AI policy.” He told reporters it was a “good sign” that Republican senators and lawmakers have spoken out because they “realize this is a threat to national security.”
Dareh Gregorian is a politics reporter for NBC News.
Brennan Leach is an associate producer for NBC News covering the Senate.

articles.title_orig: Snowden on steroids: AI agents in phones trigger surveillance fears
articles.title_zh: Snowden on steroids: AI agents in phones trigger surveillance fears
articles.content_orig:
AI agents are lurking in your phone, hoovering up your messages, pictures and emails in a privacy breach that "makes the Edward Snowden revelations look like a joke," privacy proponents are warning.
Privacy-preserving messaging app Signal has started blocking screenshots by default in an attempt to stop AI agents from reading people's screens and capturing potentially sensitive data.
The makers behind Signal — which is considered the industry gold standard for confidential, encrypted messaging — warned that Google, Apple and Microsoft are integrating autonomous agents "deep" within their device operating systems, allowing the agents to bypass privacy safeguards in individual apps.
"The ability for billions of devices to permanently spy on their users makes the Edward Snowden revelations look like a joke," Udbhav Tiwari, head of strategy and global affairs at Signal, told POLITICO, referring to the 2013 disclosures about mass U.S. government surveillance.
Tiwari warned that governments with a penchant for surveillance could ask tech firms for access to data gathered by AI agents, skipping the need to break end-to-end encryption or install malware on someone’s device.
Apple, Google and Microsoft declined to comment on Signal’s claims.
Itxaso Domínguez de Olazábal, policy adviser at European digital rights group EDRi, called for "serious limits" on what AI agents can access. "There is something deeply worrying about a not-so-far-away future where the companies controlling our operating systems can effectively decide how much privacy we are allowed to have, even when we deliberately choose services designed to protect it," she said.
"Probably the most sensitive device in your entire life is your phone. If it gets nicked, the person stealing your phone is not going to have access to your whole life. We're undoing all those safeguards by inviting AI agents onto these devices," said Gus Hosein, executive director of privacy NGO Privacy International.
Signal is pushing for makers of operating systems to provide tools so apps can opt out of AI data access and processing.
Operating system level AI agents have already launched in many countries globally, but rollout is slower in the EU. Apple has cited the EU’s digital competition rulebook as a key hurdle for the rollout of its latest AI virtual assistant features.
Social media giant Meta is also rolling out its own AI agent, Muse, which launched in the United Kingdom on Tuesday . Digital regulators including the Information Commissioner's Office already warned last month that AI agent products “may amplify and accelerate risks” to consumers. The British privacy authority said this week that Meta committed to a “voluntary monitoring and reporting scheme” to enable ongoing scrutiny, and that it is preparing new guidance on how privacy law applies to AI agents.
Meta has said its new AI agent is “private, safe and secure by design," and that it has "engaged constructively" with regulators.
Beyond the most high-risk situations, there are concerns AI agents could also gather data to repurpose for things like AI training or targeted advertising.
Ireland’s powerful privacy regulator, which oversees data protection policies at Apple, Google, Meta, Microsoft and other tech giants, is also cracking down on how "third-party" data is hoovered up by AI agents and repurposed.
Third-party data pertains to someone who isn't directly dealing with the AI agent; for example, you send a message or holiday pictures to a friend without knowing they've given an AI agent permission to access their messages.
The Irish Data Protection Commission intervened in the past month to stop Elon Musk-owned X from feeding AI models with third party data collected by its Grok Bot, POLITICO first reported .
Irish Data Protection Commissioner Niamh Sweeney said last week that it is "much more challenging" to inform third parties about their data being processed, or give them a chance to opt out, when they have “no idea” that their data could also be scooped up.

articles.title_orig: China unveils new space mission crew, with a Pakistani astronaut set to board its space station
articles.title_zh: China unveils new space mission crew, with a Pakistani astronaut set to board its space station
articles.content_orig:
Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged in Please refresh your browser to be logged in
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
China has announced the crew for the upcoming space launch to its Tiangong space station , including a Pakistani astronaut, who will be the first foreigner to board the orbiting outpost.
Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, who served as a pilot in the Pakistan Air Force, will board China’s Shenzhou 24 spacecraft powered by the Long March 2F rocket along with Chinese colleagues Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi, the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) announced on Tuesday.
The trio is scheduled to launch from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre in northwest China at 8.18am local time on Wednesday, the agency said.
Shenzhou-24 will be China's 18th crewed launch and marks the first joint space flight mission conducted by Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of Beijing’s crewed space mission programme .
Mr Ali, 40, would spend about a week aboard the Chinese space station as a payload specialist and return to Earth aboard the Shenzhou 23 spacecraft, along with crew members Zhang Zhiyuan and Lai Ka-ying, returning after their six-month rotation.
“I’m not flying for myself; I carry the name of Pakistan on my shoulder, the hope of 250 million Pakistanis,” he told reporters at a press briefing on Tuesday.
The Pakistani astronaut hoped space cooperation between the two Asian countries would go from one astronaut in one flight to multiple joint missions to the Moon, Mars and beyond.
Mr Ali has trained for seven months since he was selected in April, including learning Mandarin for better communication with his crewmates.
“The labels and operating instructions aboard the spacecraft and space station are all in Chinese, and the Pakistani astronaut began training with virtually no foundation in the language," Mr Hongbo said.
On board the space station, Mr Ali would conduct scientific projects in the fields of biotechnology and materials, as well as an in-orbit experiment on photosynthetic microorganisms, Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported.
“To every child who’s watching while I’m in orbit, look up at the sky and remember that I am up there with your dreams,” he said.
All facilities and equipment are in good condition for Wednesday’s launch, CMSA said.
The three-module Tiangong space station was completed in late 2022, and ever since, rotating six-month-long missions have kept the orbiting outpost constantly crewed ever since.
China hopes. to double the size of the space station in coming years, and facilitate more joint missions with crews from other countries.
This comes as the US and China are locked in a space race to the Moon, with both countries aiming to land boots on the lunar surface by 2030.

articles.title_orig: China investigates Politburo member and Shanghai party chief Chen Jining
articles.title_zh: China investigates Politburo member and Shanghai party chief Chen Jining
articles.content_orig:
China’s anticorruption watchdog has launched an investigation into the top Chinese Communist Party leader in Shanghai and member of the elite Politburo, Chen Jining, according to state media.
The 62-year-old, who is the fourth member of the top leadership body to be probed since last year, is suspected of “severe violations of discipline and laws”, the Xinhua news agency reported. The phrase is a common euphemism for corruption.
As part of President Xi Jinping’s widening anticorruption campaign , three Politburo members from the 24-member body have already been removed in its current term, which began in 2022, including General Zhang Youxia and He Weidong, both senior members of the Central Military Commission that oversees the armed forces, and Ma Xingrui, a provincial party secretary.
Mingda Qiu, a senior analyst at the Eurasia Group, said Chen’s investigation was part of an “unprecedented pattern”.
“The takedown again shows that Xi Jinping’s anticorruption campaign has no limits,” he said.
Chen earned a doctorate in environmental engineering at Imperial College London and rose through the ranks at China’s elite Tsinghua University to become its president.
He entered government as China’s environmental protection minister before becoming the mayor of Beijing. In 2022, he joined the Politburo as the party boss of Shanghai, China’s financial hub.
The post is one of China’s most prestigious provincial-level positions, often serving as a springboard to top leadership roles. Xi briefly served in the role in 2007 before joining the Politburo’s Standing Committee, the country’s highest decision-making body.
China’s second-ranking official, Prime Minister Li Qiang, as well as Vice President Han Zheng, also held the Shanghai post before moving into central leadership roles.
In a separate development, Liu Min, a senior official at the Ministry of Science and Technology, has also been placed under investigation for suspected “serious violations of party discipline and national laws”.

President Donald Trump has revealed what he told Jensen Huang right before the Nvidia chief executive was reinstated, following a 'spy' sex scandal that had forced him to resign.
'I talked to him [Jensen Huang] last night,' Trump told CNBC in an interview. 'I said, 'Jensen, just promise me one thing: You're going to work hard.
'You got brain, you got everything going. You're going to work hard, and if you work hard, there's nobody can beat you'.'
Nvidia's board of directors announced on Monday that the recently ousted boss would return to his position at the helm of the AI giant.
It prompted a stunning rally in Nvidia's shares – adding more than 30 per cent or nearly $1trillion (£763billion) to its value.
'The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO,' Trump wrote on social media.
The White House confirmed that Trump called in to the company's board of directors to advocate for Huang's return to leadership.
Huang's whirlwind firing and rehiring after multiple reported affairs, two with Nvidia subordinates and another with an alleged Chinese spy named Alice Huang, have prompted a tumultuous few weeks for the AI firm and the US economy .
'The Country needs Jensen's leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy,' Trump said in a statement shortly after the company announced Huang's rehiring

'He's apologized for indiscretion, which was unfortunate. That was probably that's what brought it to such a level, because sex sells fellas!' Trump said in a CNBC interview Monday morning.
'Now, [Jim] Cramer would not know that because he's a very, very, very committed person. But sex sells.'
Trump also claimed that Huang's wife, Lori, 64, has also decided to stand by her husband despite his infidelity.
'He's got a very, very, very good wife, and they've worked it out,' Trump told The New York Times. 'She's a fantastic woman.'
The president separately posted a meme on his Truth Social showing Huang holding up a red bra in a wild re-imagining of the iconic photo after Trump was shot by a would-be assassin in 2023.
Huang met his wife of 41 years at Oregon State University, when they were paired as lab partners in an electrical engineering class. He was 17 at the time.
The couple had already welcomed their two children, Madison and Spencer, by the time he co-founded Nvidia in 1993.
Both Madison and Spencer now hold key positions within high-priority business units at the company.
Lori is the president of the family's $9 billion charitable foundation and often accompanies her husband to events.
As the US's predominant AI company and microchip manufacturer, Nvidia has ballooned to become one of the most expensive US companies and a leader of cutting-edge computational development in the race against China for tech supremacy.
The recent string of damaging stories about Huang's personal conduct contributed to the company hemorrhaging over $1 trillion in market cap.
But the stock roared back to life, gaining over 25 percent on Monday following Trump's announcement that the company is not a national security risk.
'The Country needs Jensen's leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy,' Trump said in a statement shortly after the company announced Huang's rehiring.
'The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security.

'The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.'
Huang is still the subject of an internal Nvidia investigation into his affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based data firm Megaspeed, which has been of particular concern within the administration.
There are suspicions that Alice Huang used her role at Megaspeed to convince the Nvidia boss to allow the sale of advanced chips to the Singapore-based firm before those same chips were used by Chinese AI firms, helping them effectively circumvent an export ban.
US officials noted that the Megaspeed executive speaks English well and has relationships with executives at the highest levels of the AI chip industry
'NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company's compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security,' Trump said.
Nvidia said in its announcement on Monday that the probe into the 'foreign intelligence effort' will proceed and that the CEO 'fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it.'
Additionally, the Nvidia boss is scheduled to testify before Congress on December 1 about the affair with the suspected spy.
The company has since established a national security and export control committee to identify possible compliance and security risks.
Trump has grown close with the Nvidia boss during his second term, repeatedly hosting Huang at the White House for ritzy state dinners and inviting him on state visits to China and the United Kingdom.
The president has also traded millions worth of Nvidia stock.
The Republican has made at least 108 transactions worth between $27.2 million and $97.9 million during his second term, according to a CNBC analysis of the president's Nvidia stock trades.
His official filing puts his Nvidia holdings at anywhere between $12.5million to $58million (£10million to £45million) at the end of 2025. The White House always says independent managers run Mr Trump's portfolio.
Huang returned Monday to Nvidia headquarters in Silicon Valley, and employees gathered in the building's atrium loudly cheered him on.
'I am going to be a better CEO the second time around,' Huang said.
The CEO, who will also serve as Nvidia president, said in a statement that he was 'honored' to return to the company and that he resumes the responsibility 'with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.'
He thanked board Chairman Harvey C Jones and interim CEO Colette Kress, who will return to her role as chief financial officer, as well as Nvidia's executive staff for their leadership during the brief period of disorder.
'I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support,' Huang´s statement said.
'Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can´t wait to get back to work.'
Fox News host Jesse Watters warned Trump that he will face massive Democratic backlash – and maybe even an impeachment attempt – after he saved the embattled Nvidia CEO.

'The Democrats will likely use the scandal to impeach,' he then warned.

articles.title_zh: Stock futures decline as Nvidia pulls back, giving back part of Monday’s rally: Live updates
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia's remarkable stock comeback isn't done yet now that Jensen Huang has returned as CEO , CNBC's Jim Cramer said Monday.
"It's terrific to have this admittedly tarnished national treasure back leading Nvidia," the " Mad Money " host said. "It's kind of a miracle given the board's insistence that he would never get the CEO job again. But it's a miracle that saved the Nasdaq which, in turn, saved the market, at least for now."
Nvidia shares soared 31.5% on the news, fueling a broader rally in AI infrastructure stocks. The S&P 500 jumped 4.7%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite surged 6.5%, with both indexes posting their best days since April 2025. Monday's rebound erased nearly all of Nvidia's decline following Huang's Nov. 12 resignation amid reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including one involving an alleged Chinese spy. Before the rally Monday, the stock had fallen in all trading sessions since his departure.
"Jensen's only one man, and Nvidia is only one company," he said. "But the truth is that Jensen is the linchpin that holds the AI solar system together, and Nvidia is the biggest beneficiary."
Cramer argued that Huang's reinstatement removes a major source of uncertainty for investors, strengthening the case for a higher valuation. The chipmaker delivered blockbuster quarterly results last week, raising its revenue growth outlook to 75%, but the results did little to stem the sell-off as investors remained concerned about its leadership.
"If it weren't for the Jensen overhang, and the insistence that Jensen could never come back, ... I think the stock would have been up significantly on that quarter," Cramer said.
Still, Cramer cautioned that Huang's return doesn't erase the broader headwinds facing Nvidia. Growing political opposition to data center construction following the midterm elections could slow AI infrastructure expansion, while uncertainty surrounding chip sales to China threatens a potential source of demand. Meanwhile, a more hawkish Federal Reserve has pressured technology stock valuations as investors brace for higher interest rates.
Those challenges, Cramer argued, make it difficult to justify a return to the $213 level Nvidia traded at before The New York Times first reported about Huang's relationship with a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence on Oct. 29. But with Huang back at the helm and the company's growth outlook intact, he said the stock deserves a higher valuation. The stock currently trades at roughly 10 times earnings estimates for Nvidia's fiscal 2028, according to FactSet.
"There is just no way that, with the return of Jensen, this stock deserves the same 10 times price to earnings multiple," Cramer said.
"These things are subjective, of course, but to start, let's say this stock deserves to trade at twelve times next year's earnings estimate, which would make this a $199 stock," Cramer said. "That's my target."
